newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's Samper raps worldwide drug use.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's Samper raps worldwide drug use.

text.p: On the eve of another possible U.S. blacklisting of Colombia for failing to win its fight against drugs, President Ernesto Samper said Thursday that rich drug consumer countries were the real losers.
"An international report by the United Nations office on drugs proves, not only that consumption is growing, but that there is a bigger number of permanent consumers," Samper said.
He said Colombia, the world's largest producer of cocaine and an increasingly important source of heroin, was doing everything possible to win the supply side of the drug war.
But he stressed that too little was being done to fight end-use consumption.
Without a more concerted effort to fight drug use, the links in the global drug chain threaten to go forever unbroken, Samper said in a speech to police commanders from across Colombia.

"Needless to say, the Colombian people feel we have the right to demand that industrialised countries act with the same forcefulness that we are acting with on our links in the chain on their own links," he said.

In an annual report to Congress, U.S. President Bill Clinton must say by March 1 whether Colombia should remain on a list of so-called "decertified" countries that are failing to pull their weight in the international anti-drug fight.
Colombia was put on the list in March 1996. Decertification for a second consecutive year could entail painful economic sanctions that Clinton fell short of imposing a year ago.

Samper did not refer directly to the U.S. decision in his speech. But he said: "We are depressed, disheartened and outraged by the steps being made in some parts of the world toward the legalisation of drugs."
Pointing a finger of blame at the United States, he said Colombia could neither understand nor approve of "the legalisation of marijuana for medicinal use in Arizona or California."
